artDirection.target: Family-friendly open-world realism with stylized readability, believable proportions, intentional materials, and mechanically or anatomically plausible construction.
artDirection.recognitionRule: Every asset must be immediately recognizable from its silhouette and major functional components before color or labels are considered.
artDirection.hardEdgesRule: Hard edges, square forms, flat panels, and angular geometry are welcome when the real object or approved town style calls for them. The prohibition is crude placeholder construction, not geometric sharpness.
artDirection.detailRule: Hero and close-range assets require secondary forms such as seams, fasteners, vents, supports, handles, trim, lenses, panels, joints, or service access appropriate to the object.
artDirection.plausibilityRule: Vehicles, machinery, buildings, furniture, creatures, and people must have a coherent physical structure. Decorative futuristic styling cannot replace the functional anatomy or engineering of the object.
artDirection.townReferenceRule: Town materials, density, silhouette, and atmosphere must follow docs/WORLD_VISUAL_REFERENCE_BIBLE.md and the applicable town blueprint.

prohibitedShortcuts: generic primitive fallback for an unsupported family
humans assembled from cylinders and spheres without credible anatomy, clothing, hands, feet, face structure, and rigging
monsters or animals represented by stacked circles, repeated blobs, or disconnected primitive piles
vehicles without a readable chassis, passenger cabin, propulsion system, lighting, access panels, and stable stance
hover vehicles that are only a floating box or toy saucer
buildings that are only an undecorated rectangular shell when the specification requires a functional facade
one-material assets when the real object clearly contains distinct materials
unlabeled generic output quietly substituted for a requested asset
Roblox-like filler, toy-block proportions, or third-grade collage styling
random neon on assets whose town profile does not call for neon

starter-town.style: welcoming, lived-in American city realism; warm brick, stucco, concrete, patched asphalt, painted metal, ordinary civic and residential materials

fishing-harbor.style: working coastal municipality; weathered wood, painted metal, rope, wet surfaces, practical marine hardware, salt-worn details

rich-hills.style: luxury hillside realism; stone, stucco, glass, landscaped masonry, premium vehicles, gated civic and residential architecture

techtown.style: sleek cyberpunk smart city; dark brushed metal, black composite panels, tinted glass, polished concrete, controlled cyan, magenta, violet, and electric-blue lighting

casino-strip.style: dense entertainment district realism; layered signage, hotel facades, service infrastructure, parking, backstage logistics, controlled spectacle

dungeon-outskirts.style: grounded dark-fantasy frontier; stone, timber, iron, leather, practical guild and settlement construction around a colossal descending dungeon gate

obby-canyon.style: large-scale canyon adventure infrastructure; engineered platforms, bridges, rescue equipment, rock integration, believable supports and safety systems

starline-city.style: glamorous production city with real backstage labor; theaters, studios, hotels, hills, apartments, warehouses, lighting rigs, and service corridors

aqualume.style: advanced inhabited underwater city; pressure-rated structures, curved glass, coral-integrated architecture, current-powered transit, marine engineering, luminous but functional materials
avoid: structures with no pressure or anchoring logic

shared-world.style: cohesive family-friendly open-world realism matching the owning town and gameplay role
